subject: Targeted tenant traffic reassignment — EU/APAC egress disruption (action & postmortem)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:12:00 -0000
Subject: Targeted tenant traffic reassignment — EU/APAC egress disruption (action & postmortem)

Hi Samantha,

Quick update and an ask of your ops team. We observed a degraded egress path from two cloud regions affecting a subset of tenants with EU and APAC routing preferences between 07:40–08:05 UTC this morning. Impact: increased latency and a small number of timed-out requests for your EU tenants (primarily eu-west-3) during that window.

What we did: our on-call team executed a targeted traffic reassignment to alternate egress nodes and enabled a short-term prefixed KV cache bypass to reduce retries. Impacted requests should now be routing through the secondary path.

Action required from ACME: please confirm whether your tenant(s) observed persistent errors after 08:10 UTC and, if possible, share any logs for the 07:30–08:20 UTC window. We attached a short runbook that lists verification steps your network team can run — it includes curl examples and expected response headers.

Attachments: reroute-runbook-v1.pdf (verification steps, curl examples)

I will follow up with a concise post-incident summary once we have the memo ready. Sorry for the disruption — we know how sensitive latency is for your checkout flows.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 17:04:00 -0000
Subject: Resolve & post-incident summary: EU/APAC egress disruption — actions completed

Hi Samantha,

Thank you for the traces — that helped. Summary and actions completed: 

Incident summary (short):
- Window: 2027-05-04 07:40–08:05 UTC.
- Cause: transient egress path degradation inside thirdpartycloud's eu-west fabric (packet drops to the primary egress node). Thirdpartycloud confirmed a short fiber flapping event with their edge provider; they applied the fix at 08:03 UTC.
- Impact: elevated latency and intermittent 504s for tenants with EU/APAC egress preference; ACME saw ~1.2% failing checkouts during the window.

Actions we executed:
- 07:46 UTC — triggered targeted reassignment to secondary egress nodes for affected tenants.
- 07:50 UTC — enabled aggressive retry/timeout adjustments for proxied requests to minimize client-visible errors.
- 08:03 UTC — thirdpartycloud repaired their fiber and primary egress returned to stable.
- 08:10 UTC — we reverted temporary retry settings and removed the KV cache bypass; normal routing resumed.

Customer impact & billing:
- We have no evidence that client requests led to duplicate successful charges. ACME traces confirmed retry semantics that can cause duplicated attempts but our payment gateway idempotency keys prevented duplicate settlements. Still, Olga's team completed a quick scan of transaction logs for the 07:30–08:20 UTC window and found zero duplicate settlements.

Session affinity:
- Jordan confirms we preserved X-Forwarded-For and cookie-based affinity; the reassignment maintained TCP source preservation at the transport layer, so session continuity should not have been affected.

Attachments & artifacts:
- Attached: postmortem-summary-ACME-20270505.pdf (concise timeline and remediation actions), reroute-runbook-v1.pdf, route-validation-checklist.csv
- Postmortem doc (full): https://drive.redwood.com/teams/postmortems/ACME-20270505

Recommended next steps for ACME:
1) If you have any sign of customer reports beyond the traces you uploaded, send them to ops@redwood.ai and we'll escalate immediate checks.
2) Optional: opt into our long-tail caching profile to reduce sensitivity to short-term egress flaps (we can enable it for a trial window).
3) Join a 30-minute sync with our engineering lead if you'd like a technical walkthrough: I can coordinate for Thu 2027-05-06 afternoon UTC.

Apologies again for the interruption. We're opening a follow-up ticket with thirdpartycloud and will include you in status updates. Please reply to confirm you received the postmortem and whether you'd like the trial caching profile enabled.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
